card.name: Spots just before a drug name or dose figure
card.fires_on: Small joining words and punctuation right before a named drug or a dose number, such as 'co-administration of', 'drugs that act', or a space after 'up to'. Seen mostly in interaction and pregnancy text.

modes.label: Before an interacting drug
modes.description: The word 'of' or a comma sits just ahead of a calcium channel blocker name in an interaction list.

modes.description: The verb 'act' in 'Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system' in fetal toxicity warnings.

modes.label: Space before animal dose amounts
modes.description: The space after 'up to' just before mg/kg dose figures in animal reproduction studies.

card.writes: It lowers the odds of the word dose or dosage coming next, so a drug name or number is favored instead.
card.plain: It marks the spot just before a drug name or amount is about to appear, mostly in interaction and pregnancy warnings.
